newsitem.title: POLAND: Warta cuts motor liability insurance rise.
newsitem.headline: Warta cuts motor liability insurance rise.

text.p: Poland's second largest insurer, TUiR Warta SA, cut its planned increase in motor liability insurance premiums to about 27 percent from an earlier announced 33-percent average, Warta's spokesman said on Monday.
"Warta has reduced its rise by 5-7 percentage points as of Monday from the earlier-announced rise of 30-35 percent," Jacek Likowski told reporters.

He said it revised its plans due to expectations that the finance ministry would issue a regulation requiring insured persons to contribute part of damages payments, which would reduce the amount paid by insurers.
He added that if the regulation was not implemented, Warta could return to its earlier-announced increase in premiums.
Last week Poland's largest insurer, Powszechny Zaklad Ubezpieczen SA (PZU), reduced its increase in obligatory motor liability insurance premiums to 33 percent from an earlier-announced 43 percent.
